summary: Feed s116_double is degraded: IDS 1 Gbps port is hit by 3.80 Gbps microbursts (380% capacity) causing 3.5% genuine TCP packet loss (54/1552). Slicing ruled out as cause - drops are buffer overruns from overload, blinding IDS detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating too much traffic onto a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load-balancing. 1ms microbursts peak at 3.80 Gbps (380% of port capacity, 2 overloaded intervals), overflowing broker egress / IDS ingress buffers.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port cannot ingest bursts, buffers overflow and traffic is dropped before inspection. IDS misses exploits, loses state, and detection coverage collapses during bursts.

recommended_fix.why: Hash-based load balancing across 3-4 IDS ports/instances spreads 3.8 Gbps bursts so no single 1 Gbps port exceeds 80% capacity, eliminating burst drops while preserving flow symmetry required by IDS.

findings.root_cause: Genuine packet loss, not slicing artifact. Check measured TCP segments by IP header length and ruled out slicing. 3.48% loss (54 of 1552 TCP packets) is downstream effect of the 3.8 Gbps overload - port buffers tail-drop packets during bursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS with needs_both_directions=true and needs_full_payload=true loses TCP sequence continuity. Reassembly fails, signatures and anomaly detection miss attacks, and 3.5% of flows have blind spots.

recommended_fix.why: Same overload root cause; distributing traffic via load-balanced tool group prevents buffer overruns that create TCP gaps, restoring complete flows to IDS without filtering needed traffic.
